title: Defence products manufacturer VTDS signs strategic technology pact with Czech Republic's DEUS Automation
content:
• Defence products manufacturer Vijayan Trishul Defence Solutions (VTDS) signed a strategic technology pact with the Czech Republic's DEUS Automation a.s.
• The collaboration aims to strengthen long-term defence manufacturing, specifically in the small-calibre ammunition sector in India.
• DEUS Automation a.s., part of the STV Group of the Czech Republic, will provide advanced manufacturing technology to VTDS for small-calibre ammunition production in India.

title: US-Iran war news LIVE: Deal on Strait of Hormuz is close, not enough to open waterway, says Iran
content:
• Iran and Oman are "very close" to an agreement on a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been largely shut since the US-Iran conflict began in late February, though the IRGC insists it will only reopen if the US "fully" accepts Tehran's conditions.
• On 5 August, US Deputy Secretary of Defense Steve Feinberg sent a letter to major US defence companies, urging them to accelerate the production and delivery of key weapons systems due to concerns about shortages exacerbated by the Iran war.
• US Central Command (US CENTCOM) on Saturday redirected 53 commercial vessels and disabled/boarded two each as part of the "blockade against Iran," while allowing over 30 ships passage for humanitarian aid.

title: UAE accuses Iran of missile attack on its vessel in Strait of Hormuz; no casualties reported
content:
• On Saturday, August 8, the UAE accused Iran of a missile attack on an ADNOC-affiliated vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
• The Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy route, previously carried about one-fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments.
• Iran and Oman are reportedly 'very close' to an agreement on a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran demanding conditions like the lifting of US sanctions for its full reopening.

title: Keralam Lower Primary School Teacher rank holders eat grass in protest — why are they demonstrating for over a month?
content:
• Lower Primary School Teacher (LPST) rank holders have been protesting for over 34 days outside the Kerala Secretariat, expressing anger over delayed appointment orders from the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC).
• The government has reportedly asked for two months to address the concerns of the protesting LPST rank holders regarding their appointments.
• In July, the Kerala Home Department directed the Crime Branch to conduct a comprehensive enquiry into alleged irregularities in Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) examinations, establishing a Special Investigation Team (SIT) chaired by Inspector General of Police S Ajeetha Begum, IPS.

title: Trump’s UK grant push for ‘public education’ courses: Why US embassy’s $500,000 scheme is raising concerns
content:
• The US embassy in London has announced grants of up to $500,000 for new “public education” initiatives in the UK.
• The specific grant program is titled “Liberty Under Law: The Shared Anglo-American Tradition” and prioritizes projects promoting “freedom of speech” and “limited government.”
• Separately, the US State Department is reportedly preparing a $12 million funding package for UK organizations founded by prominent Conservative figures Jacob Rees-Mogg and Toby Young.

title: Spain begins process to replace ambassador to India over alleged financial favours: Report
content:
• Spain has initiated the process to replace its ambassador to India, Juan Antonio March Pujol, following allegations of accepting financial favours and misusing public funds.
• A key allegation against Ambassador Juan Antonio March Pujol involves personally securing a €5,000 contribution from BLS International, an Indian visa-processing company, for a cultural event in Rajasthan.
• Juan Antonio March Pujol was appointed Spain's ambassador to India in June 2024, and previously served as president of the ONUART Foundation until February 2024.

title: UPI to remain free for users; nominal MDR may apply to select merchant transactions
content:
• The "UPI and Services Steering Committee" headed by NPCI will decide on any future MDR, following the amendment of Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, via the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
• UPI will remain free for Person-to-Person (P2P) transactions and the vast majority of merchant transactions; however, nominal MDR may apply to a limited set of merchant transactions above a certain threshold.
• UPI was introduced in 2016 and made free of charge for users and merchants since January 2020; it processed 2,366 crore transactions worth ₹29.9 lakh crore in July 2026.

title: US sanctions bill makes India-US trade deal more critical, may push up import bill: Economist
content:
• The US Senate passed a Russia sanctions bill on Friday with an 86-11 vote, which could impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries, including India and China, for purchasing Russian crude oil and natural gas.
• Madan Sabnavis, Chief Economist at Bank of Baroda, stated that current crude prices are stable around USD 80, but a renewed conflict escalation could impact India's Current Account Deficit (CAD) by 0.1-0.2% of GDP.
• The proposed US sanctions legislation makes it critical for India to negotiate a trade deal with the United States, as any disruption to crude supplies could raise India's import bill and put pressure on the rupee.

title: India's resilient economy to support markets but global risks remain elevated: SEBI
content:
• India's Real GDP growth was estimated at 7.7 per cent in 2025-26, according to SEBI's Annual Report 2025-26.
• FPI equity outflows from India reached a record $19.7 billion during 2025-26.
• The IMF projected India's growth at 6.5 per cent for 2026-27, compared with global growth of 3.1 per cent.

title: Fresh 100% US tariff threat could add to India's inflation, CAD pressures: CareEdge
content:
• The US has threatened to impose 100% tariffs on countries continuing to purchase Russian oil.
• In July, Russian oil accounted for approximately 50% of India's total crude imports.
• Sachin Gupta, Chief Ratings Officer at CareEdge Ratings, stated that if crude reaches $110-120 per barrel, India's current account deficit could "easily double" from last year's level.
